The package exports FileSystem, Reader, Writer, and the TypeScript FileInfo interface. Browser I/O methods return promises. Operations on an individual reader or writer must be awaited sequentially.

Method Result and behavior FileSystem.connect() Promise<FileSystem> rooted at the current origin. Initializes WASM on the first connection. catFile(path, start?, end?) Promise<Uint8Array>. End is exclusive; negative offsets count from the end. Bounds are clamped to file size. pipeFile(path, data) Promise<void>. Replaces file contents and commits before returning. Accepts Uint8Array. open(path) Promise<Reader>. Opens an existing file for reading. writer(path) Promise<Writer>. Opens a replacement write; parent directories must exist. info(path) Promise<FileInfo>. Returns file or directory metadata. ls(path = "") Promise<FileInfo[]>. Lists directory children, sorted by name. A file path returns that file’s metadata as a one-item array. mkdir(path, parents = false) Promise<void>. Creates a directory. With parents, creates missing parents. rmdir(path) Promise<void>. Removes an empty directory. rmFile(path) Promise<void>. Removes a file. cpFile(src, dst) Promise<void>. Reads the source into memory and replaces the destination. free() Releases the WASM filesystem object. Stored files remain.

Method Result and behavior read(size) Promise<Uint8Array>. Reads up to size bytes and advances the cursor. Returns an empty array at EOF. seek(position) Promise<number>. Sets an absolute nonnegative byte position and returns it. close() Promise<void>. Releases the browser file reference. Repeated close is allowed. free() Releases the WASM reader object. Offsets and read sizes must be finite safe integers; read sizes must be nonnegative. Reads and seeks after close fail.

Method Result and behavior write(data) Promise<void>. Appends a Uint8Array to the pending replacement. commit() Promise<void>. Publishes the replacement and closes the writer. An empty replacement truncates the file. abort() Promise<void>. Discards uncommitted bytes. Safe after abort or commit. free() Releases the WASM writer object and schedules abort if unfinished. Writes and commits after commit or abort fail. Dropping a JavaScript reference does not guarantee prompt cleanup; explicit abort is available for application cleanup.

FileInfo has name: string, size: number, and type: "file" | "directory". File metadata from info and ls also includes lastModified, expressed as milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Directories have size zero and no modification timestamp. Rejected I/O promises contain an Error with a string code. Mapped codes include not_found, permission_denied, not_supported, not_a_directory, is_a_directory, and invalid; other browser failures use the backend’s fallback error classification. A missing WASM asset or module initialization failure may instead produce a loader error without a backend code.

Browser exports are available for wasm32-unknown-unknown: API Contract Opfs::new().await Returns FsResult<Opfs> for the current origin. Opfs::writer(path).await Returns FsResult<OpfsWriter> for a replacement write. OpfsWriter::write(&mut self, bytes).await Writes a pending chunk. OpfsWriter::commit(&mut self).await Publishes and closes. OpfsWriter::abort(&mut self).await Discards pending bytes. Drop schedules this cleanup. Opfs implements fsspec_rs::AsyncFileSystem, including ls, info, mkdir, rmdir, rm_file, cp_file, cat_file, and pipe_file. open_async returns Box<dyn AsyncFsFile> with read, seek, info, and close. The legacy open method returns NotSupported because it requires a blocking file handle. Browser futures run on the owning JavaScript event loop and may be non-Send. Configure fsspec_rs with default-features = false; native Tokio runtime adapters are not used.

OPFSFileSystem implements fsspec.AbstractFileSystem and is registered under opfs. It provides open, info, ls, mkdir, makedirs, rmdir, rm_file, rm, cp_file, and cat_file, plus fsspec’s derived operations. local_root is the native fallback directory or None in the browser. close() frees browser state or removes the native directory; the filesystem also supports a context manager. Browser open supports read and replacement write modes, including text wrappers. Native fallback uses local file modes. Browser operations require Pyodide JSPI and a registered fsspec_opfs_js module; Python setup describes the entry point and module registration. Browser setup errors never trigger native fallback.

t: How to read and write browser files
x: Open a writer when input arrives in chunks. Await each operation before starting the next operation on the same handle. const writer = await fs.writer("examples/chunks.bin"); try { await writer.write(new Uint8Array([1, 2])); await writer.write(new Uint8Array([3])); await writer.commit(); } finally { await writer.abort(); writer.free(); } Call commit() to publish the replacement bytes. abort() discards an unfinished replacement and is safe after commit. See write behavior for the empty-file and concurrent-write limitations.

t: How to read and write browser files
s: Read a range or use a handle
x: Read bytes 1 through 2 with an exclusive end offset: await fs.catFile("examples/chunks.bin", 1, 3); // Uint8Array [2, 3] await fs.catFile("examples/chunks.bin", -1); // Uint8Array [3] For repeated reads, use a reader and close it in cleanup: const reader = await fs.open("examples/chunks.bin"); try { await reader.seek(1); const bytes = await reader.read(2); console.log(bytes); } finally { await reader.close(); reader.free(); } When finished, call fs.free() to release its WASM allocation. This does not delete stored files.

t: How to use OPFS from Python
x: Install the package in native Python and retain one filesystem instance for related operations: import fsspec with fsspec.filesystem("opfs") as fs: print(fs.local_root) # Temporary directory, with a RuntimeWarning at construction. fs.pipe_file("example", b"temporary bytes") assert fs.cat_file("example") == b"temporary bytes" Each instance gets a different temporary directory. Closing it deletes that directory; garbage collection also schedules temporary-directory cleanup. Native files are not shared with a browser or another filesystem instance. Keep important data elsewhere. OPFS paths remain relative to that root, including paths beginning with /. Dot components, backslashes, NUL characters, and symbolic links resolving outside the root are rejected. This path confinement does not protect against another native process modifying directories during an operation.

Browser storage and write behavior OPFS gives a web application a private filesystem managed by the browser. The root belongs to the current origin and browser profile, so another origin or profile has different files. OPFS does not expose arbitrary files from the user’s operating system. The Rust implementation calls browser APIs through WebAssembly. JavaScript and Rust callers use the same async operations. Blocking Rust file handles are unsupported because browser I/O completes through the JavaScript event loop. The Python adapter uses Pyodide’s JSPI support to suspend synchronous fsspec calls while that event loop processes I/O. On a server it warns and uses a temporary local directory; it cannot access a browser profile’s files. Why writes require commit A writer uses the browser’s writable file stream to prepare replacement bytes. Commit closes that stream and publishes the replacement. Aborting or dropping an unfinished writer discards the replacement, preserving the previous contents of an existing file. Opening a writer for a new path may create an empty file immediately. A writer uses the browser’s writable file stream to prepare replacement bytes. Commit closes that stream and publishes the replacement. Aborting or dropping an unfinished writer discards the replacement, preserving the previous contents of an existing file. Opening a writer for a new path may create an empty file immediately. Aborting that writer can leave the empty entry. The filesystem therefore does not provide atomic create-if-absent or the guarantees needed to publish immutable table manifests. Commit also has a cancellation boundary: once the browser has started closing the writable stream, dropping the Rust future cannot guarantee that publication stops. Applications need to account for an uncertain result if they stop waiting at that point. Concurrent writers follow the browser’s behavior. This backend adds no compare-and-swap, writer fencing, conflict detection, or cross-file transactions. A chunked writer avoids collecting the complete input in application code; it does not impose a hard limit on the browser’s internal buffers. pipeFile accepts a complete input buffer, and cpFile currently buffers the complete source.

Files persist across page reloads, but browser quotas, eviction, profile deletion, and clearing site data affect storage lifetime. A successful persistence request reduces eviction risk; it does not protect against explicit deletion. Requesting persistence and maintaining recoverable copies are application responsibilities. The current browser test suite runs against Chromium and checks reload persistence, ranges, read handles, directory behavior, and write commit/abort. Other browsers and worker-only synchronous access handles are outside that tested scope.

import { FileSystem } from "fsspec-opfs"; const fs = await FileSystem.connect(); await fs.mkdir("tables", true); await fs.pipeFile("opfs://tables/example", new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3])); const bytes = await fs.catFile("tables/example", 1); // [2, 3] const entries = await fs.ls("tables"); const writer = await fs.writer("tables/example"); try { await writer.write(new Uint8Array([4, 5])); await writer.write(new Uint8Array([6])); await writer.commit(); } finally { await writer.abort(); // Safe after commit; otherwise discards the write. writer.free(); } const reader = await fs.open("tables/example"); await reader.seek(1); const chunk = await reader.read(2); await reader.close(); reader.free(); fs.free(); catFile accepts optional start and end byte offsets, including negative offsets from the end. info, ls, mkdir, rmdir, rmFile, and cpFile operate on paths relative to the origin’s OPFS root. mkdir(path, true) creates parents. rmdir removes empty directories. Errors expose a code such as not_found, permission_denied, is_a_directory, or invalid. Serve the package’s dist/pkg directory alongside its dist/esm or dist/cdn directory so the WASM URL resolves. The CDN entry is an ES module.

[dependencies] fsspec_opfs = "0.1" fsspec_rs = { version = "0.4.1", default-features = false } use fsspec_opfs::Opfs; use fsspec_rs::AsyncFileSystem; let fs = Opfs::new().await?; fs.mkdir("tables", true).await?; fs.pipe_file("tables/example", &[1, 2, 3]).await?; let bytes = fs.cat_file("tables/example", None, None).await?; The crate is browser-only. The Python adapter registers opfs with fsspec: in Pyodide it uses this browser backend through JSPI; native Python warns and uses an isolated temporary local directory. See the Python setup guide. Blocking Rust filesystem handles, worker-only synchronous access handles, and registry integration are not provided.

A writer publishes bytes only when commit() completes. abort(), Rust Drop, and JavaScript free() discard uncommitted replacement bytes. Explicitly abort writers in application cleanup; JavaScript garbage collection is not timely. Once commit has started, dropping its future cannot guarantee cancellation. Opening a new path for writing can create an empty file before commit. This backend does not claim atomic create-if-absent, conditional writes, conflict detection, or manifest publication guarantees. Concurrent writes follow browser behavior. pipeFile buffers its input; use a writer for chunked output. cpFile currently buffers the source file. OPFS requires a secure context (HTTPS or localhost), a supporting browser, and storage permission. Files persist across reloads within the same origin and browser profile. Storage quotas, browser eviction, and clearing site data can remove them. Applications needing persistence should request it through navigator.storage.persist() and inspect the result.
